clue.text: Small sum — not CE pew rent

indicators.note: rent here is the past tense of rend, torn apart, so the letters before it are pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchgoer quibbles that a tiny charge for a pew is not Church of England practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment for the pew, but it means torn: the eight letters of NOT CE PEW are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin worth two old pennies was a trifling amount of money.

clue.text: County town later abandoned by english

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters of the word before it run riot

explanation.surface: An English visitor leaves a provincial town at some later date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as left behind, but it is the anagram signal on LATER, giving TRALE, then E is added. TRALEE is the county town of Kerry in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tralee is the administrative centre of County Kerry.

clue.text: Do a favour to old boy — tell tale about German

parts.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fib wraps around the abbreviation for German

parts.note: to tell a tale is to lie

explanation.surface: A former pupil helps out by spinning a story about a German.
explanation.definitionFit: To accommodate someone is to perform a kindness for them.

clue.text: Swallow flung about with energy

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something gulped down is thrown around energetically.
explanation.definitionFit: To engulf is to overwhelm and take in completely, like gulping something down.

clue.text: Instrument pumping calor gas in

indicators.note: pumping suggests forcing something through and churning it, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Bottled heating fuel is being pumped into a container.
explanation.walkthrough: Calor Gas is a British brand of bottled gas; its letters with IN rearrange to the name of the woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is a woodwind of the oboe family, an orchestral instrument.

clue.text: Fabian socialist and editor becoming entangled

parts.note: Sidney Webb was a founding figure of the Fabian Society

explanation.surface: A Fabian thinker and a newspaper editor get caught up together in some affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Sidney and Beatrice Webb were leading members of the Fabian Society, a British socialist group.
explanation.definitionFit: Something caught as if in a web or mesh is webbed in that sense.

clue.text: Imagine cultivating vines with one willing to participate

indicators.note: cultivating suggests working and turning soil, so the letters of the word after it are turned over

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
saying 'I'm on' means you are up for joining in

explanation.surface: Picture someone tending grapevines alongside an eager volunteer.
explanation.definitionFit: To envision something is to picture it in the mind.

clue.text: Finance aircraft manoeuvres

parts.note: a plane can bank, tilting into a turn
a plane can also roll, turning about its long axis

explanation.surface: Money is needed to pay for aerial stunts.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'aircraft manoeuvres' supplies two separate manoeuvres in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To bankroll a venture is to fund it.

clue.text: Covering in mayonnaise?

parts.note: the clue seems to describe smothering food in sauce, but it points to a word meaning both a bandage-like covering and a salad sauce, of which mayonnaise is one

explanation.definitionFit: A wound covering and a salad sauce share one name, and mayonnaise is an example of the sauce.

clue.text: Everything English covered in blood — it's symbolic

parts.note: everything means all
gory means bloodstained

explanation.surface: Something entirely English and bloodsoaked carries a deeper meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story whose characters and events stand for hidden meanings.

clue.text: A place to play a game in the street

parts.note: a venue is a place where a match or event is held

explanation.surface: Children look for somewhere to play a game out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad road in a town, a type of street.

clue.text: Encourage to start growing aubergine

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them
to plant something is to set it going in the ground

explanation.surface: A gardener is urged to begin raising a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggplant is the American name for the purple vegetable called aubergine in Britain.

clue.text: Old style flower for Egyptian god

parts.note: OS stands for Old Style, dates in the calendar used before the Gregorian reform
the iris is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned bloom is offered to an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the ancient Egyptian deity of the dead and the afterlife.

clue.text: Neither grave nor acute?

parts.note: it reads like a description of something neither serious nor sharp, but grave and acute are the names of accent marks over letters

explanation.definitionFit: A letter with no grave or acute mark carries no stress mark at all.

clue.text: Plain girl back to collect a grand in Eisteddfod town

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so the word for plain takes the abbreviation for a grand inside it

parts.note: a llano is a grassy plain in Spanish America
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: back means the girl's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Nell is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A plain girl comes home to pick up a thousand pounds in a Welsh festival town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to collect' puts G inside LLANO, and 'back' turns NELL into LLEN. Llangollen in Wales hosts the International Eisteddfod, a music festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Llangollen, in north Wales, hosts the annual International Musical Eisteddfod.

clue.text: Agas help to produce this if burning solid fuel?

definitions.text: Agas help to produce this if burning solid fuel?

indicators.note: burning suggests something being consumed and transformed, so the letters of the words before it change shape

explanation.surface: Kitchen ranges fuelled by coal contribute to the waste tips left by mining.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a British cast-iron range cooker; those burning coal add to the demand that piled up mining waste. The letters of AGAS HELP rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip of mining waste grows from digging the coal that such stoves burn.

clue.text: North Briton defrayed costs on island

indicators.note: defrayed is read as de-frayed, the word unravelled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A Scot covered the expenses while living on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: North Briton is an old term for a native of Scotland.

clue.text: Seat boss constructed in fireproof material

indicators.note: constructed means built or put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A manager's chair is made of a fire-resistant substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral formerly used for fire-resistant insulation.

clue.text: Result of sewing hair on to little chap?

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair
Titch is British slang for a very small person

explanation.surface: Someone stitches a wig onto a small boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on to' places the tresses before the small chap. A lockstitch is the stitch made by a sewing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A lockstitch is the interlocking stitch produced by a sewing machine.

clue.text: Involved in share issue, male's to save hard

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within, so the abbreviation for male goes inside the share issue

parts.note: scrip is an issue of certificates or extra shares
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man caught up in a new share offering must economise.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be thrifty and economise strictly.

clue.text: Copper climbing chimney, one reaching clouds

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so the word for chimney is reversed

parts.note: lum is a Scots word for chimney
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A policeman climbs up a chimney stack until he reaches the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns LUM, a Scottish word for chimney, into MUL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumulus is the heaped, fluffy type of cloud, and its plural ends in -i.

clue.text: Heraldic beast makes wife awfully nervy

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of the word after it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mythical creature leaves a married woman terribly jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a winged two-legged dragon found on coats of arms.

clue.text: Understand gun is to be given to that woman

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: A firearm is to be handed to a particular woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather can mean to infer or conclude from what one hears.

clue.text: About to keep busy and take up residence again

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to occupy someone is to keep them busy

explanation.surface: Someone about to find work moves back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'About' is RE and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a home is to live in it, and doing so a second time is re-entering it.

clue.text: Hostility of new men to Information Technology unknown

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters of the word after it are remade

parts.note: y is a letter used in algebra for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Fresh recruits show antagonism towards computing, a field they do not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is mutual antagonism or ill will.

clue.text: Poet endlessly imbibing dry vermouth — it's a pose

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the shortened poet takes the drink inside him
endlessly means the poet's name loses its last letter

parts.note: W. H. Auden was an English poet
TT means teetotal, so not drinking alcohol
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A poet drinking dry vermouth is merely striking a pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts AUDEN to AUDE, and 'imbibing' puts TT and IT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike an attitude is to adopt a posture or stance.

clue.text: Drive around Northern Ireland fine? Possibly

indicators.note: around means the word for drive surrounds the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

parts.note: to drive something forward is to push it

explanation.surface: A motorist touring Northern Ireland wonders if the weather will be fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks 'fine' as one example: to fine someone is one way to penalise them.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing a monetary penalty is one way of penalising an offender.

clue.text: A daughter likely to encounter charge for alteration

parts.note: apt means likely, as in apt to happen
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A girl may well be faced with a fee for altering a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaption is a modification made to suit new conditions.
